bullets.title: Democratic midterm sweep triggers AI/data-center selloff; renewables surge
bullets.body: Democrats won both House (231+ seats) and Senate (54+ seats), triggering a sharp sector rotation: solar/renewables jumped 4-12% (FSLR +7.3%, ENPH +4.0%) while data-center/AI infrastructure names fell 2-13% pre-market. Power stocks tied to Texas (TLN, VST, CEG) dropped 6-8% as Democrats swept the Texas governor race. S&P 500 futures were +0.84% to 7,660.5 with 10-year yields -3 bps to 4.93%.

bullets.title: Election creates data-center permit moratorium risk in TX, GA — ~45% of planned US capacity at risk
bullets.body: Democratic state wins in Texas and Georgia are expected to trigger data-center permitting moratoriums, affecting an estimated 45% of planned U.S. capacity according to Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley. Texas's new governor is expected to impose a moratorium pending the Jan–May 2027 legislative session. Projects already under construction (e.g., HUT's Beacon Point I) are largely protected, but new permits and financing for Phase II expansions are at risk.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure earnings broadly strong: AMD, ANET, SMCI all beat and raise big
bullets.body: AMD guided Q4 revenue to $17B (+4% vs. Street), with data center revenue up 97% YoY to $8.5B in Q3 and CY27 revenue growth flagged at >80%; Helios GPU ramping at Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle. Arista Networks beat with Q3 topline +58% YoY and guided FY27 growth of 38-40%, well above the ~30% consensus. Super Micro beat its own pre-announcement with Q1 EPS $1.81 vs. $1.23 consensus and raised FY27 revenue guidance to $72-82B.

bullets.title: DDOG's flat Q4 guide (-17% pre-mkt) is key read-across for cloud software
bullets.body: Datadog beat Q3 revenue by $53M (5%) with 35% YoY growth, but guided Q4 to only ~25% growth — a material deceleration even after accounting for the Q3 beat — implying near-flat sequential revenue vs. the normal +7-8% quarterly pace. The miss reflects large-customer optimization headwinds. SNOW fell 5.1%, MDB -4.6%, NET -3.9% in sympathy.

bullets.title: ORCL cancels $7B Tencent chip deal under Trump administration pressure; stock -4.9%
bullets.body: Oracle canceled a $7B chip-leasing arrangement with Tencent after pressure from the Trump administration. The move is a direct read-through on geopolitical risk around US-China AI supply chains and limits Oracle's near-term capacity expansion options.

bullets.title: Meta raises $15B bond offering for AI infra; hyperscaler off-balance-sheet commitments up 90% in 6 months
bullets.body: Meta raised $15B in a five-part bond offering earmarked for AI infrastructure. Separately, tech giants' off-balance-sheet AI commitments have surged 90% in six months to $3.2T in data center and power contracts, underscoring the scale of the buildout even as political headwinds emerge.

bullets.title: Anthropic's custom chip design effort is IPO-linked — threatens EDA incumbents (SNPS, CDNS)
bullets.body: Anthropic is showcasing in-house chip design capabilities to IPO investors, posing a competitive threat to EDA vendors Synopsys and Cadence. This follows a broader trend of hyperscalers verticalizing silicon design to reduce dependence on third-party EDA tools.

bullets.title: BKNG: strong Q3 but Q4 guided +1-3% room nights on geopolitical disruptions
bullets.body: Booking Holdings beat Q3 gross bookings ($54.5B vs. $53.3B est.) but reported a $900M revenue reduction tied to an FTC complaint. Q4 guidance implies room-night growth of only 1-3% YoY, 400 bps below expectations, citing Middle East conflict, European civil unrest, and US macro softness. ABNB and EXPE seen as better-positioned given heavier US mix.

bullets.title: WULF/Google backstop $19B Anthropic data-center lease in Kentucky — non-TX buildout accelerating
bullets.body: TeraWulf secured Google credit support for debt financing underpinning a ~$19B, 20-year Anthropic lease at its Justified Data Campus in Kentucky (401 MW, full ramp by early 2028). The EPC agreement with Fluor adds guaranteed-maximum pricing. WULF is viewed as insulated from Texas political risk given Kentucky location.

bullets.title: Texas gubernatorial flip puts HUT's Beacon Point II at permitting risk; stock -10% pre-mkt
bullets.body: HUT 8's Beacon Point Phase I (3Q27 delivery) is under construction and likely protected, but Phase II (2Q28) financing and new TCEQ permits are at risk from an anticipated Texas data-center moratorium pending the Jan–May 2027 legislative session. HUT's $1B buyback authorization and $1.07B undrawn revolver provide some offset; ROTH maintains Buy at $108 PT and views Texas risk as a timing issue rather than permanent impairment.

bullets.title: Hedgeye flags phase transition: sell high-beta, buy long bonds and defensives into Q1-Q2 2027 slowdown
bullets.body: Hedgeye sees a post-Q3 2026 economic peak underway, with SPX, COMPQ, and RUT all in bearish trend signals. The recommended playbook: sell high-beta equities (NVDA, META, AMZN, GOOGL, NFLX bearish) on green days, add long-duration bonds (ZROZ, BNDD), low-vol equities (USMV), and staples (XLP). UST 30-year yield is in a bearish trend phase for 3 weeks with the 10-year showing lower highs.

bullets.title: Euro area headline inflation jumped to 4.0% on energy; core steady at 2.54%
bullets.body: Euro area October headline CPI rose 0.2 ppts to 4.0% YoY, driven by energy up 20.8% YoY; core inflation held at 2.54%, near the 2.55% forecast, with services at 3.30%. JPMorgan trimmed its Q4 euro area growth forecast to 1.25% from 1.5% on softer October PMI (51.7 revised, France collapsing to 46.6). Core inflation expected to peak at 2.8% in early 2027.

bullets.title: ChatGPT now at 20% of Google search query volume — monetization risk building
bullets.body: JPMorgan's tech sketch notes ChatGPT queries have reached 20% of Google search volume, raising concerns about long-term search market share and monetization for Alphabet. GOOGL also reportedly expanding voluntary global buyout offers as it accelerates AI spending.

bullets.title: SMCI beats with triple-digit revenue growth but gross margin compression looms in H2
bullets.body: Super Micro reported Q1 EPS $1.81 vs. $1.23 consensus on $19.95B revenue (+14% vs. $17.53B est.); raised FY27 guidance to $72-82B from $65-72B. The key overhang: Citi flags implied H2 FY26 gross margin compression to 11.8-12.2%, and one customer represents 44% of revenues.

bullets.title: US power demand projected 6x by mid-2040s driven by AI — NextEra planning $60B/yr capex 2027-32
bullets.body: NextEra CEO described a sixfold increase in US electricity demand through the mid-2040s from AI data centers, reshoring, and electrification. NextEra plans ~$60B in annual capital spending 2027-2032. The CEO prefers supplying hyperscalers over owning data centers; Google signed a 25-year power deal supporting the Duane Arnold reactor restart. SMR commercialization is not expected until the mid-2030s.

bullets.title: SHOP misses buyside GMV targets; AI-driven orders converting 64% better than organic
bullets.body: Shopify's Q3 GMV grew 29.5% YoY, missing buyside expectations of 33-34%, with revenue +32% vs. 34-35% estimates. Q4 guide maintains low-thirties revenue growth. Notably, AI-driven orders on Shopify are growing 3.3x and converting 64% more often than organic traffic — a structural positive even as near-term numbers disappointed.

bullets.title: Broad Russell 2000 earnings season: 41% market cap reported, beating EPS by 4.3%
bullets.body: With 514 of 2,000 Russell 2000 stocks (41% of market cap) reporting, aggregate earnings are running 4.3% above expectations (4.1% ex-financials) and revenues 2.3% above (2.7% ex-financials). Russell 2000 is +13.3% YTD, outperforming S&P 500 by 2.8%.

bullets.title: WTI crude -2.1% to $94; Trump signals no imminent Iran strike, Middle East oil exports recovering
bullets.body: WTI fell 2.06% to $94.11 in pre-market despite bullish API inventory data. Trump signaled no immediate plans to strike Iran ('we're getting everything we want'), dampening war-premium. Middle East oil exports rose 10% MoM in October but remain 2.4 MMBopd below pre-war February levels.

bullets.title: UBER Q3: 20% FXN gross booking growth; Mobility decelerated on Middle East and driver supply
bullets.body: Uber reported Q3 gross bookings of $59.8B (+20% FXN), slightly above guidance. Mobility decelerated to 17% FXN (from 20% in Q2) due to Middle East conflict (75 bps headwind) and tighter international driver supply. Delivery accelerated to 23% FXN with frequency at all-time highs; Ads hit $10B ARR. Q4 GBs guided $63.25-65.25B with ~1pt FX headwind; AV fleet targeted at 2,000 units by end-2027.

bullets.title: Enterprise IT spending stable but not accelerating; AI ROI scrutiny rising into 2027
bullets.body: An enterprise IT survey cited in OPCO's morning note shows a stable spending environment but limited acceleration into 2027, with AI spending shifting toward measurable ROI. This is consistent with the DDOG guide miss and DT's (Dynatrace) slipped large deals, though both companies maintain platform consumption growth above 20%.
